key_insight: For D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr on DSS 2205 in 1 M H2SO4, the 190 mm spray distance produced the densest coating and the best corrosion resistance.
engineering_relevance: Optimizing spray distance is a practical lever for improving coating integrity and extending the service life of stainless-steel components in acidic industrial environments.
method: D-gun spray Cr3C2–NiCr onto DSS 2205 at 170, 180, and 190 mm stand-off distances.
Evaluate corrosion behavior in 1 M H2SO4 using OCP, EIS, and potentiodynamic polarization.
evidence_signal: Porosity decreased from 2.84% at 170 mm to 1.38% at 190 mm, and the 190 mm coating showed the lowest corrosion rate (0.113 mmpy) versus 2.60 mmpy for the uncoated substrate.
watch_item: The optimum distance was determined under one electrolyte and room-temperature test conditions, so performance may differ under other acids, temperatures, or service wear conditions.
paper_title: Effect of spray distance in D-gun sprayed Cr3C2–NiCr coatings on DSS 2205 in acidic environments
